h: Wands at the ready: planning the tour
p: Getting there is straightforward. If you're coming by train, head to Watford Junction, where a dedicated shuttle bus runs to the studio. Driving is easy too, with parking on site, but leave time for traffic around Watford if you've got a timed slot to make.

Once you're inside, the highlights come thick and fast. Walk into the Great Hall, wander down Diagon Alley, stand on Platform 9 3/4 next to the Hogwarts Express and brave the Forbidden Forest. The huge, detailed model of Hogwarts Castle near the end is a real jaw-dropper, and plenty of grown-ups get a bit emotional seeing it.
Outside on the Backlot you'll find more big set pieces, including the Knight Bus and Privet Drive. It's also where you can try a glass of Butterbeer, a rite of passage for most fans.

Allow plenty of time. Most visitors spend several hours inside, and there's no need to rush, so book a slot that doesn't squeeze you for time. Comfortable shoes are a must, and bring a fully charged phone because you'll take far more photos than you expect.
The shop at the end is enormous and very tempting, so set a budget with the kids before you go in.
